tone_statements.citation: Kutsch Lojenga, Constance. 1996. Participatory research in linguistics. Notes on Linguistics 72: 13-27. Dallas: Summer Institute of Linguistics. (reproduced in ERIC ED401726, 'Notes on Linguistics, 1996', pp. 74-88)
tone_statements.quote: As with the segmentals, nouns and verbs should be treated separately since the tones or tonal melodies are not necessarily the same for these two word classes. In our Ngiti experience, we found that there were five possible tone patterns on VCV nouns: L.L, M.M, M.H, H.L, L.LM, whereas verb infinitives only displayed three tone patterns: M.L, M.M, and M.H. On the basis of our findings with nouns and verbs, we first established the number of level tones in the language, the presence or absence of falling and rising tones, and we made lists of tone minimal pairs.

sources.citation: Reh, Mechthild. 1996. Review of Kutsch Lojenga, Ngiti: A Central Sudanic Language of Zaire. Afrika und Übersee 79: 148-150.
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent. Reports the grammar's structure (Kap. 2 phonologische Struktur, Kap. 3 phonologische Prozesse, Kap. 4 Töne) and stresses the high functional load of tone: 'Diese Beschreibung macht die hohe funktionale Bedeutung der Töne im Ngiti sehr deutlich. Mit ihrer Hilfe werden nicht nur viele Lexeme voneinander unterschieden (S. 95), sondern sie sind auch ein zentrales Mittel der Verbalflexion und -derivation' (p. 149).

sources.quote: As with the segmentals, nouns and verbs should be treated separately since the tones or tonal melodies are not necessarily the same for these two word classes. In our Ngiti experience, we found that there were five possible tone patterns on VCV nouns: L.L, M.M, M.H, H.L, L.LM, whereas verb infinitives only displayed three tone patterns: M.L, M.M, and M.H. sources.locator: p. 24 (Notes on Linguistics 72, 1996), section 4.4 'Tone'; ED401726 = p. 12
sources.note: Methodology paper whose worked example is the author's 1988-93 Ngiti fieldwork; section 4.4 'Tone' reports first-hand that VCV nouns show five tone patterns L.L, M.M, M.H, H.L, L.LM and verb infinitives three (M.L, M.M, M.H), i.e. three level tones (L, M, H) plus a rising LM contour, with many tone minimal pairs; grammatical tone in the verb system deferred to later analysis (full system in the 1994 grammar ch. 4). Also states Ngiti has only open syllables V and CV with short vowels and a 9-vowel ATR system.
